_comment: Defines what counts as a 'young listed company'. Tune freely - run.py reads this on every run.
min_revenue_note: A listed operating business you could read an annual report about. Below roughly $10m of trailing revenue you are into nanocaps whose shares are too thin to enter or leave without moving the price.
max_data_age_note: How old the newest tagged figure may be. A company can file on time while its XBRL series stops years earlier, usually after a tag change SEC never framed. 20-F filers report annually and get the longer window.
min_series_density_note: Fraction of the quarters the series spans that are actually reported. Growth measured across holes is not growth.
sic_blocklist_note: Blank checks, unit investment trusts, REITs, asset-backed issuers, commodity dealers - not operating companies.
ownership_note: Form 3/4/5 filings read per company. Each is one request, so this is the main cost driver of a deep scan.
